chunks: Al-Saffar from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya said: Abu Burdah ibn Rajaa' told me, saying:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is your view regarding the purchase of the land of the Khurasan tax?' He said: 'And who sells that, while it is the land of the Muslims?'
I said: 'The one who holds it in his possession sells it.' He said: 'And what does he do with the tax of the Muslims?'
Then he said: 'There is no harm. He buys his right from it, and the right of the Muslims shifts to him, and perhaps he will be stronger upon it and more enduring with their tax than he is.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on buying tax land (Ard al-Kharaj) from the government?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the pre-modern practice of *Iqta'* or tax farming, where the state sold the right to collect land tax (*Kharaj*) to private individuals. While initially questioning the logic of alienating communal assets, he permits the transaction on the pragmatic grounds that the buyer, now bearing the burden of collection, may become more efficient or enduring in managing the Muslims' obligations than the state itself. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing effective governance and the welfare of the community (*Maslaha*) in administrative matters.
